parsed.strategy: Bet that the fastest-moving policy variables in the Oct 12-Nov 13 window are defense budgets (German spend +30% YoY, NATO glidepath), nuclear-fuel security (DOE HALEU task order, uranium term contracts), critical-minerals nationalism (US government equity stakes in MP and Trilogy Metals), and CHIPS/industrial policy (Intel's 10% stake, TSMC/ASML capex). Every name has a confirmed or primary-sourced dated event inside the window, so relative P&L is driven by real prints and policy headlines, not theme drift. I would be wrong on a de-escalation headline (Ukraine ceasefire progress, US-China trade detente, or a court striking the government equity-taking authority) that compresses the whole geopolitical-risk-premium complex at once.
parsed.objective: Maximize relative P&L vs the Bloomberg WLS index from 2026-10-12 to 2026-11-13 through policy- and geopolitics-driven global names with in-window catalysts.
